cache_validation: input and configuration digests plus complete run manifest

formula.command_issue_interval_formula: ceil(tCK / model_cycle_ns); each physical channel issues row commands on its own replicated DRAMSim3 command lane
formula.command_model: request completion is measured from actual READ/WRITE issue; row conflicts explicitly schedule PRE then ACT before the data command, while tWR/tRTP/tRAS and PRE-to-ACT constrain recovery
formula.read_to_precharge_formula: ceil((AL + tRTP) * tCK / model_cycle_ns); bundled HBM config omits tRTP, so DRAMSim3 default tRTP=5 applies
formula.read_to_write_formula: ceil((RL + burst_cycle - WL + tRTRS) * tCK / model_cycle_ns)
formula.transfer_note: burst/block transfer is modeled separately by transfer_cycles, so BL is not duplicated in CL/CWL completion latency

memory_ablation.admission_policy: FIFO and batch-class share one global admission clock; at most four 64-byte blocks enter all channel controllers per paper cycle, while each channel independently enforces the 32-entry read queue and 32-entry write buffer
memory_ablation.command_queue_source: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini cmd_queue_size=8; the request-level controller bounds each bank command queue to the same depth

command_trace.policy: every PRE, ACT, READ, and WRITE event is stored in a reversible chunked stream; the validator independently reconstructs event and command totals, checksum, edge samples, channel-lane spacing, tCCD/turnaround, and bank recovery

memory_ablation.coordinator_input_policy: The required FIFO baseline has no active-window resource cap: each admission cycle selects one ready Edge/Input/Weight/Output port and admits up to four consecutive blocks subject only to the same transaction and command queue capacities used by batch-class. Positive fifo_active_windows values are diagnostic counterfactuals, not paper evidence. Batch-class changes only request ordering and assembles batch-local Edge > Input > Weight > Output streams with same batch/class open-row continuation.
memory_ablation.coordinator_input_source: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Figure 9 identifies four Edge, Input, Weight, and Output request sources; it does not specify four unfinished 2 KiB windows. Section 4.5.2 attributes the optimization to priority-based request reordering and low-bit channel/bank mapping.
memory_ablation.coordinator_issue_width_source: derived from the paper profile peak interface width: floor(256 bytes/cycle divided by 64 bytes/block)

dram_timing.command_issue_interval_formula: ceil(tCK / model_cycle_ns); each physical channel issues row commands on its own replicated DRAMSim3 command lane
dram_timing.command_model: request completion is measured from actual READ/WRITE issue; row conflicts explicitly schedule PRE then ACT before the data command, while tWR/tRTP/tRAS and PRE-to-ACT constrain recovery
dram_timing.read_to_precharge_formula: ceil((AL + tRTP) * tCK / model_cycle_ns); bundled HBM config omits tRTP, so DRAMSim3 default tRTP=5 applies
dram_timing.read_to_write_formula: ceil((RL + burst_cycle - WL + tRTRS) * tCK / model_cycle_ns)
dram_timing.transfer_note: burst/block transfer is modeled separately by transfer_cycles, so BL is not duplicated in CL/CWL completion latency

memory_ablation.fifo_window_release: diagnostic-only when fifo_active_windows is positive; the required profile is unbounded
memory_ablation.low_bits_source: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Section 4.5.2: channel and bank identifiers use lower address bits

occupancy_trace.policy: every admission records per-channel read/write occupancy before and after mutation; a terminal zero snapshot lets the validator infer all intervening dispatch counts from zero and independently recompute peaks, capacity violations, totals, histograms, edge samples, and checksum

memory_ablation.priority_order_source: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Section 4.5.2 executes requests batch-by-batch: all requests from the current batch, including its lower-priority classes, precede high-priority requests from the next batch
memory_ablation.row_first_layout_basis: one row-sized block span stays in one bank, then the collapsed mapping advances channel and bank fields in the order represented by rorabgbachco
memory_ablation.row_first_source: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini selects address_mapping=rorabgbachco. The collapsed request-level baseline therefore keeps every contiguous row span in one bank; it does not add an unsupported adjacent-bank striping factor.
memory_ablation.topology_source: HyGCN reports 256 GB/s HBM1. The bundled DRAMSim3 HBM1_4Gb_x128 profile is one 8-channel 128 GB/s stack, so the paper profile replicates that timing and queue topology across two stacks rather than inventing a faster per-channel command rate.
memory_ablation.transaction_queue_source: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini sets unified_queue=False and trans_queue_size=32; DRAMSim3 therefore allocates an independent 32-entry read_queue and 32-entry write_buffer in every channel controller

scope.validated: Fig. 15 layer-0 AE-only sparsity and Fig. 16-17 layer-0 request-level microarchitectural effects for GCN

graph_partition.fit_disclosure: Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed were all exposed before this version; the 5 MiB scheduler cap and the 14 paper rows are reported as a calibrated fit, not independent hold-out validation
graph_partition.historical_exposure: Review v4 evaluated all three datasets at 4, 5, and 6 MiB before Review v5; no dataset in this repository remains unexposed for scheduler-cap selection
graph_partition.policy: fixed dataset-independent scheduler occupancy cap below one physical ping-pong half
graph_partition.source: HyGCN Section 4.3.2 requires the destination interval and its aggregation results to fit the on-chip Aggregation Buffer; the paper does not publish the simulator's interval occupancy, so this request-level model reports the fixed scheduler cap separately from the 16 MiB physical capacity
